producer_report.summary: The reader now gets a compact form of each default, and the new `root-cause` default is in `defaults.toml`. No budget was raised and BRIEF.md is untouched. `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` all pass. I could only confirm that `cargo test --locked` exited with success; its full output was too long to read. `DefaultsModel::render()` now shows each default's id, classes and first sentence, through a new `Default::gist()`. The producer and verifier briefs still use the full statement, and the budget test passes. I added no `defaults.toml` field, so the installed gate still parses the file. The compact form alone was not enough: the reader set came out at 1802 of 1800 tokens, because most statements were already one sentence. I therefore split five existing statements into a gist sentence plus a detail sentence (`buy-first`, `public`, `verified`, `evidence`, and one more). The wording is the same apart from punctuation and capitalisation, so the meaning is unchanged, and the briefs show the full text.

checks_run.note: The first run failed the reader budget by 2 tokens (1802 of 1800). It passed after the statement splits. Exit status only; the full output was too long to read.

open_issues: The `root-cause` source citation and wording come from the brief's description; I could not check them against BRIEF.md.
The headroom under the 1800 budget is small and I did not measure it. The test prints the estimate only on success.
I put the `root-cause` entry between `small` and `verified`, and gave it applies_to `*`, which is my choice.
mistakes: I made a pointless rename of defaults.toml and a bare restore before editing it. The file is back and nothing was lost.
I first capitalised `cargo` while splitting the `tested` statement, then restored the original wording.
learnings: Most existing default statements were single sentences, so a first-sentence rule alone saved nothing; the statements had to be restructured.
The reader budget test uses an estimate of ceil(bytes/3) and was at the limit.
The briefs code already used the full statement, so briefs.rs needed only a new test.
docs/design.md does not exist; the relevant design text is in docs/design/athena-v0.md section 4.4.
desires: A way to read the full test output when it is long, since my Grep on the saved output was blocked by the path policy.
A way to read BRIEF.md, to confirm the root-cause wording and source.
